properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony's idea, 2026-08-15, framed by him as aspiration rather than intent — his own words end "but I don't think we are there yet", preserved here as part of the idea rather than trimmed off it.

HIS WORDS: "in some designs, actual design reviews are done and official direction to proceed and other formal docs are required (coming from the US Air Force and US Space Force, documentation is required — maybe we can eventually get to where the graph tracks authorizations to proceed or other official acquisitions documents are in the graph and organizations trust the graph to hold such docs and therefore, keeping external docs is no longer needed — but I don't think we are there yet)."

DELIBERATELY DISTINCT FROM `rule:design-information-lives-in-the-graph-not-in-documents`, which the guard named because this node cites it. THAT RULE GOVERNS THIS REPOSITORY and is settled and enforced. THIS IS A QUESTION ABOUT THE PRODUCT, in a domain where a document is not a convenience: a signed authorisation to proceed is what makes work lawful to start, and whether an organisation will rely on a graph instead is a question about trust, audit and legal standing rather than about storage. The rule can hold while this stays open, and it does.

WHAT ALREADY POINTS THIS WAY, so the starting position is not zero: `Contributor` with `AUTHORED_BY role: approver` records whose sign-off a node carries and when (`acted_at`); `Decision` with `status: accepted` records that something was settled and by whose word; `DesignEpoch` records when; and this project has already settled that rendered pages are ONLY projections of the graph rather than documents in their own right. An authorisation is structurally an approver plus a date plus a scope plus a decision — all four of which the schema can already say.

WHAT IS MISSING IS NOT VOCABULARY, AND THAT IS THE INTERESTING PART: it is EVIDENCE and NON-REPUDIATION. The graph can record that somebody approved something; it cannot today demonstrate to a third party that they did, that the record has not moved since, or that the approver had the authority. A `status: accepted` written by an agent and one written by a general are the same bytes.

THE OPTIONS:

(a) DO NOTHING; FORMAL DOCUMENTS STAY EXTERNAL and the graph points at them with `Artifact.location`. HONEST TODAY, costs nothing, and matches his own concession that a pointer "might be okay". COUNTER: it is exactly the arrangement the no-documents rule was made to end, so the product would be telling consumers to do what this project forbids itself.

(b) THE GRAPH HOLDS THE AUTHORISATION AS TYPED NODES, the signed document stays external as evidence. Cheap, mostly expressible already. COUNTER: it splits the record — authority in the graph, proof in a file — which is the worst of both for an auditor.

(c) THE GRAPH HOLDS THE BYTES TOO. A signed PDF is precisely "what the graph cannot hold inline", the sentence `cap:content-store` was built around — BUILT, VERIFIED, AND DISCONTINUED on his word on 2026-08-09 for zero use across three projects (`dec:the-content-store-is-discontinued`). ⭐ THIS WOULD BE THE FIRST REAL USE THAT DISCONTINUATION SAID DID NOT EXIST. COUNTER, and it is his own from that decision: bytes in a repo grow without bound, and in flo2 could reach terabytes needing backup, security and per-project separation — all MORE true, not less, for controlled or classified acquisition documents.

(d) THE DOCUMENT IS DERIVED FROM THE GRAPH — the official record is generated as a rendering, so there is one source and the document is an output rather than an input. Consistent with the settled doctrine that pages are only renderings. COUNTER: a rendering is not a signature. Something must still capture the act of approval by a person with authority, and that act happens outside reflow2.

⚠️ THE HONEST BLOCKER, stated so it is not rediscovered: whether an organisation trusts a graph is not a feature reflow2 can build. It is earned through audit, retention policy, access control and someone accepting liability. Everything above is necessary and none of it sufficient, and a version that shipped the mechanics while implying the trust would be the most damaging overclaim this project could make.

NOT ESTABLISHED: whether any real programme would accept it; what standard would have to be met (none has been named); and whether this is one question or two — TRACKING authorisations, versus BEING the authoritative record.
properties.name: IDEA — in acquisition work the formal documents ARE the artefact: design reviews, authorisations to proceed, official direction. Could the graph hold them well enough that an organisation trusts it and stops keeping external docs?
properties.rationale: Recorded via the brainstorm skill at `proposed`, options with counters beside them, nothing promoted. Started as a new node rather than merged into the rule after the guard named it: the rule governs this repository and is settled, while this asks whether the product could carry legal-weight documents for someone else — different scope, different decider, and merging them would bury a product question inside a house rule. His \"I don't think we are there yet\" is preserved inside the idea, because a later reader would otherwise read the aspiration as a plan.
